newsitem.title: FRANCE: Petrol bombs target French National Front town.
newsitem.headline: Petrol bombs target French National Front town.

text.p: Police arrested two men in the French town of Vitrolles on Friday after petrol bombs overnight hit the town hall and the office of the far-right National Front which won the town's municipal elections this week.
No one was hurt but a fire was started at the party office, police said.
The attacks were the latest in a series of violent incidents which began on Sunday when Catherine Megret, the wife of the Front's number two Bruno Megret, won the election run-off.
The election drew wide attention in France and abroad as commentators said it showed new progress by the xenophobic party which wants to expel millions of foreigners from France.
Vitrolles is the fourth French town controlled by the Front after it won Toulon, Orange and Marignane in 1995.
Megret stood for office after her husband was disqualified for spending beyond legal limits in a previous poll.
She is due to take office on Sunday, but unconfirmed reports said she might herself stand down in favour of the number two on her list who is a local resident.
The Megret couple were ineligible to vote in Vitrolles since they live in Paris. They ran their campaign from a local hotel.
Police said they were drafting reinforcements into Vitrolles to prevent more violence during the Sunday handover.

The Vitrolles vote helped prompt a march by some 4,000 French artists and supporters through Toulon on Thursday to combat a drive by its National Front mayor to sack a left-wing theatre director and wind up his cultural centre.
The arts establishment has clashed repeatedly with the Front in the party's southern bastions, denouncing censorship in libraries and at cultural events.
